scores.why: Accessibility maps exist, but here the verdict fits your own wheelchair, every fact has a weight that fades with age, conflicts are shown openly, and an A4 sheet acts as a scale for AI door measurement.
Quality of life and urban mobility with open OSM data and Kraków tram stop data; a licence model aimed at the city.
Realistic 5-photo owner audit, embeddable badge, moderation; live API returns real stops. Cold start is a risk: most showcased venues are sample data.
Clean, high-contrast, accessibility-first UI with text-size and contrast modes, verdicts by shape as well as colour, automated accessibility checks.
About 10k lines of source plus 2.6k lines of tests across 40 files, database migrations, accounts, admin, disputes, real AI with a mock fallback, live demo.

projects.built_during_event: yes: 73 commits from 3 Oct 13:43 to 4 Oct 09:52 CEST
strengths: Evidence-based trust model: source weighting, decay, open conflicts
weaknesses: Mostly demo venues; coverage depends on uptake
red_flags: About 15 feature commits in 30 minutes suggests agent-driven bulk generation (disclosed)
projects.verdict: A tight, well-executed and well-designed quality-of-life product with honest data handling; the most convincing all-round entry.

scores.why: Reporting local problems is familiar (Kraków already has 19115); it stands out with automatic routing to the responsible institution from public registries, merging duplicates into one case, and AI 'after' images for proposals.
Squarely public services and urban data: parcel registry lookup, geocoded institution offices, a catalogue of proven social initiatives, emails to offices.
Deployed production instance with sign-in, Polish and English, onboarding tour and email delivery; classifier evaluation honestly reports 80.8% accuracy.
Distinctive bold outline style, map clusters, guided onboarding; no app screenshots in the repo.
About 25k lines of source across several services plus 5.9k lines of tests with 226 test functions, 14 migrations, CI/CD with Docker images.

projects.verdict: An engineering-heavy, very relevant civic platform; a moderate idea saved by excellent execution.

scores.why: Ambitious drone search-and-rescue command centre for floods: fan-shaped sectors, wind-aware search routes, a probability map from rivers and buildings, live weather to ground unfit drones.
Crisis response is in the brief, but this is a defence and emergency-services command tool, not day-to-day city operations.
Drones, sensors and image recognition are entirely simulated; only the planning part with real weather and map data is usable today.
Very polished dark command-centre UI: drone camera over real satellite imagery, flight readouts, AI analysis panel, procedure overlays.
About 18k lines of TypeScript, reports export and a working demo, but the 56 tests claimed in the documentation do not exist and about 5k lines are generic admin pages.

projects.verdict: The most visually impressive and imaginative entry, but simulated and loosely tied to Smart City, with an unverifiable build history.

calibration_note: The top two are within 1.5 points; the drone project's wow factor is held back by weak category fit and an unsupported test claim.
